name: Microsoft Agent 365 Trigger
desc: Use the Microsoft Agent 365 Trigger node to receive messages from Microsoft Agent 365 and respond with AI-powered agent capabilities. This node allows n8n to act as the backend for your Agent 365 agents

name: MiniMax
desc: The MiniMax node connects n8n workflows to MiniMax AI models. Use it to generate images from text prompts, synthesize speech, create videos from text or images, and send messages to MiniMax language models

name: Model Selector
desc: The Model Selector node dynamically selects one of the connected language models during workflow execution based on a set of defined conditions. This enables implementing fallback mechanisms for error handling or choosing the optimal model for specific tasks

name: Moonshot Kimi
desc: The Moonshot Kimi node connects n8n workflows to Moonshot Kimi AI models. Use it to send prompts and receive model responses, attach images to messages, or analyze images with an image-analysis model

name: OpenAI
desc: Use the OpenAI node to automate work in OpenAI and integrate OpenAI with other applications. n8n has built-in support for a wide range of OpenAI features, including creating images and assistants, as well as chatting with models

name: Auto-fixing Output Parser
desc: The Auto-fixing Output Parser node wraps another output parser. If the first one fails, it calls out to another LLM to fix any errors

name: Item List Output Parser
desc: Use the Item List Output Parser node to return a list of items with a specific length and separator

name: Structured Output Parser
desc: Use the Structured Output Parser node to return fields based on a JSON Schema

name: Perplexity
desc: Use the Perplexity node to automate work in Perplexity and integrate Perplexity with other applications. n8n has built-in support for messaging a model

name: Reranker Cohere
desc: The Reranker Cohere node allows you to rerank[^1] the resulting chunks from a vector store[^2]. You can connect this node to a vector store

name: Contextual Compression Retriever
desc: The Contextual Compression Retriever node improves the answers returned from vector store[^1] document similarity searches by taking into account the context from the query

name: MultiQuery Retriever
desc: The MultiQuery Retriever node automates the process of prompt tuning by using an LLM to generate multiple queries from different perspectives for a given user input query

name: Vector Store Retriever
desc: Use the Vector Store Retriever node to retrieve documents from a vector store[^1]

name: Workflow Retriever
desc: Use the Workflow Retriever node to retrieve data from an n8n workflow for use in a Retrieval QA Chain or another Retriever node

name: Sentiment Analysis
desc: Use the Sentiment Analysis node to analyze the sentiment of incoming text data

name: Text Classifier
desc: Use the Text Classifier node to classify (categorize) incoming data. Using the categories provided in the parameters (see below), each item is passed to the model to determine its category

name: Character Text Splitter
desc: Use the Character Text Splitter node to split document data based on characters

name: Recursive Character Text Splitter
desc: The Recursive Character Text Splitter node splits document data recursively to keep all paragraphs, sentences then words together as long as possible

name: Token Splitter
desc: The Token Splitter node splits a raw text string by first converting the text into BPE tokens, then splits these tokens into chunks and converts the tokens within a single chunk back into text

name: AI Agent Tool
desc: The AI Agent Tool node allows a root-level agent[^1] in your workflow to call other agents as tools to simplify multi-agent orchestration

name: Calculator
desc: The Calculator node is a tool[^1] that allows an agent[^2] to run mathematical calculations

name: Custom Code Tool
desc: Use the Custom Code Tool node to write code that an agent[^1] can run

name: MCP Client Tool
desc: The MCP Client Tool node is a Model Context Protocol (MCP) client, allowing you to use the tools exposed by an external MCP server. You can connect the MCP Client Tool node to your models to call external tools with n8n agents

name: SearXNG Tool
desc: The SearXNG Tool node allows you to integrate search capabilities into your workflows using SearXNG. SearXNG aggregates results from multiple search engines without tracking you

name: SerpApi (Google Search)
desc: The SerpAPI node allows an agent[^1] in your workflow to call Google's Search API

name: Think Tool
desc: The Think Tool node is a tool[^1] that invites an agent[^2] to do some thinking before answering. Essentially, it allows the agent to reflect on the question by talking to itself before providing an answer. In particular, this is useful for complex queries that require a thoughtful response

name: Vector Store Question Answer Tool
desc: The Vector Store Question Answer node is a tool[^1] that allows an agent[^2] to summarize results and answer questions based on chunks from a vector store[^3]

name: Wikipedia
desc: The Wikipedia node is a tool[^1] that allows an agent[^2] to search and return information from Wikipedia

name: Wolfram|Alpha tool
desc: Use the Wolfram|Alpha tool node to connect your agents[^1] and chains[^2] to Wolfram|Alpha's computational intelligence engine

name: Call n8n Workflow Tool
desc: The Call n8n Workflow Tool node is a tool[^1] that allows an agent[^2] to run another n8n workflow and fetch its output data

name: Azure AI Search Vector Store
desc: Azure AI Search (formerly Azure Cognitive Search) is a cloud search service with vector search capabilities for RAG and semantic search applications. Use this node to store, retrieve, and query vector embeddings alongside their content and metadata

name: Chroma Vector Store
desc: Use the Chroma node to interact with your Chroma database as vector store[^1]. You can insert documents into a vector database, get documents from a vector database, retrieve documents to provide them to a retriever connected to a chain[^2], or connect directly to an agent[^3] as a tool[^4]

name: Databricks Vector Store
desc: Use the Databricks Vector Store node to work with Databricks Vector Search indexes in your workflows. You can run a similarity search over an index, insert documents into a Direct Access index, hand the index to a retriever connected to a chain[^1], or connect it to an AI agent[^2] as a tool[^3]. Indexes live in Unity Catalog, so the node sees only the data the credential's identity can access

name: Simple Vector Store
desc: Use the Simple Vector Store node to store and retrieve embeddings[^1] in n8n's in-app memory

name: Milvus Vector Store
desc: Use the Milvus node to interact with your Milvus database as vector store[^1]. You can insert documents into a vector database, get documents from a vector database, retrieve documents to provide them to a retriever connected to a chain[^2], or connect directly to an agent[^3] as a tool[^4]

name: MongoDB Atlas Vector Store
desc: MongoDB Atlas Vector Search is a feature of MongoDB Atlas that enables users to store and query vector embeddings. Use this node to interact with Vector Search indexes in your MongoDB Atlas collections. You can insert documents, retrieve documents, and use the vector store in chains or as a tool for agents

name: Oracle Database Vector Store
desc: Use the Oracle Database Vector Store node to interact with Oracle Database as a vector store[^1]. You can insert documents into a vector table, get documents from a vector table, retrieve documents to provide them to a retriever connected to a chain[^2], or connect directly to an agent[^3] as a tool[^4]

name: PGVector Vector Store
desc: PGVector is an extension of Postgresql. Use this node to interact with the PGVector tables in your Postgresql database. You can insert documents into a vector table, get documents from a vector table, retrieve documents to provide them to a retriever connected to a chain[^1], or connect directly to an agent[^2] as a tool[^3]

name: Pinecone Vector Store
desc: Use the Pinecone node to interact with your Pinecone database as vector store[^1]. You can insert documents into a vector database, get documents from a vector database, retrieve documents to provide them to a retriever connected to a chain[^2], or connect directly to an agent[^3] as a tool[^4]. You can also update an item in a vector database by its ID

name: Qdrant Vector Store
desc: Use the Qdrant node to interact with your Qdrant collection as a vector store[^1]. You can insert documents into a vector database, get documents from a vector database, retrieve documents to provide them to a retriever connected to a chain[^2] or connect it directly to an agent[^3] to use as a tool[^4]

name: Redis Vector Store
desc: Use the Redis Vector Store node to interact with your Redis database as a vector store[^1]. You can insert documents into the vector database, get documents from the vector database, retrieve documents using a retriever connected to a chain[^2], or connect it directly to an agent[^3] to use as a tool[^4]

name: Supabase Vector Store
desc: Use the Supabase Vector Store to interact with your Supabase database as vector store. You can insert documents into a vector database, get many documents from a vector database, and retrieve documents to provide them to a retriever connected to a chain

name: Weaviate Vector Store
desc: Use the Weaviate node to interact with your Weaviate collection as a vector store[^1]. You can insert documents into or retrieve documents from a vector database. You can also retrieve documents to provide them to a retriever connected to a chain[^2] or connect this node directly to an agent[^3] to use as a tool[^4]. name: Zep Vector Store
desc: Use the Zep Vector Store to interact with Zep vector databases. You can insert documents into a vector database, get documents from a vector database, retrieve documents to provide them to a retriever connected to a chain[^1], or connect it directly to an agent[^2] to use as a tool[^3]
